Student Outcomes & Career Paths
Welcome to Auburn University's
Biomedical Sciences Program
The Biomedical Sciences and Health Sciences majors at Auburn University provide a strong scientific foundation for students pursuing health-related careers. Both programs emphasize rigorous coursework, critical thinking, and preparation for professional pathways in health and medicine.
Biomedical Sciences is designed for students planning to pursue advanced clinical or professional programs, while Health Sciences offers a flexible, interdisciplinary approach to exploring a wide range of health-focused careers.
Together, these majors support students as they prepare for next steps through intentional advising, academic excellence and opportunities for experiential learning.
Biomedical Sciences Program
Structured curriculum designed for students interested in research or professional school. Electives include physiology, genetics and neurobiology.
Pre-professional concentrations include:
Pre-Dental
Pre-Medicine
Pre-Optometry
Pre-Pharmacy
Pre-Anesthesiologist Assistant
Health Sciences Concentration
Pre-Physical Therapy
Pre-Physician Assistant
Career Outcomes
Graduates of Biomedical Sciences and Health Sciences pursue professional school or careers in health and science fields. Potential outcomes include:
Anesthesiologist assistant
Dentist
Health educator
Healthcare manager
Medical assistant
Medical doctor
Occupational therapist
Optometrist
Pharmacist
Physical therapist
COSAM Career Services
Pursuing Innovation
Research Opportunities
Biomedical Sciences students have access to research across the College of Sciences and Mathematics and Auburn, with opportunities in areas from pharmacy to veterinary sciences. Students gain practical experience that supports graduate student and careers in health care.
COSAM Research & Graduate Studies

Program Success
Over the last four graduating cohorts (2022-2025), 84% of biomedical sciences graduates were successfully enrolled in a continuing education opportunity within six months following graduation. For the class of 2025, 88% of biomedical sciences graduates were successfully employed within six months following graduation.
96%
of graduates from biomedical sciences majors are satisfied with their first destination career outcome
90%
of biomedical sciences majors graduating in the Class of 2025 participated in one or more high-impact practice while at Auburn
98%
of graduates from biomedical sciences programs would choose to attend Auburn University again
Biomedical Sciences Testimonials
Student Success Stories
I had always thought I would be a software engineer, but over time I realized that I truly desired a career in the medical field that keeps me on my feet and engages me in a community. It wasn’t until the day of Camp War Eagle that I knew I wanted to be a dentist, and I switched to Biomedical Sciences as my major. I couldn’t be happier with my decision.
Alex Towery
Pre-Dentistry
Class of 2026
I had the opportunity to study abroad twice with COSAM! I am appreciative for how both programs focused on different elements of my career interests while immersing me in new cultures with new opportunities. I have also had the opportunity to have wonderful shadowing experiences with physicians in the Auburn/Opelika area. I especially loved observing obstetricians and gynecologists.
Cara Herring
Pre-Medicine
Class of 2025
One of the best parts of Auburn for me has been the relationships I’ve been able to develop with faculty and my peers. I’ve had the opportunity to meet some really fantastic people who strive to help others — including me — succeed in whatever it is that we set our minds to. Every time I talk to people about Auburn, I always say that coming here was the best decision I have made.
Markelle Scott
Biomedical Sciences
Class of 2027
After the first semester, I realized COSAM had a lot of opportunities for pre-med students. The pre-health advising, the newsletter and the Canvas page all felt tailored to that path. Some of my favorite classes were cell biology and genetics. The classes were challenging, and the exams were structured in a way that felt similar to MCAT questions. We were given scenarios and had to think critically, which made me feel prepared. Looking back, I feel confident that COSAM prepared me for what comes next
Miranda Correia
Pre-Medicine
Class of 2026
I’ve grown a lot because of the research requirement. The lab includes me in opportunities I never expected to have this early. Having that kind of support has pushed me to keep learning and made me think more seriously about the kind of doctor and researcher I want to be. I definitely want research to be part of my career.
John Walker
Pre-Medicine
Class of 2028

Academics
Built for what comes next
From advising and peer support to rigorous science coursework, COSAM’s pre-health model is designed to prepare students for the demands of professional school. Alumni across five health disciplines say that foundation helped them handle the pace, pressure and complexity of their next academic step.
Shaped by Auburn, called to serve
For spring 2026 graduation marshal Cammi Griffith, Auburn has been more than a place to earn a degree. It has been a place to lead, serve and prepare for a future in medicine.
Following curiosity
President’s Award winner Amy Hudson built an Auburn experience that brought together medicine, service, mentorship and the arts. In COSAM, she found the support to follow her curiosity and prepare for the next step: medical school at UAB.
